name: pdrename
description:
A ProDOS VOLUME MOUNTED WITH -o write RENAMES, MOVES AND TRUNCATES AS ProDOS 8 AND GS/OS DO, AND OTHER READERS AGREE.  /dev/sd1 is a fresh disk/pdscratch.po; /testdata/pdrename works through pdmount -M/-T and the shell, and the check script reads the volume the machine left.

ON THE SCREEN:
  PDMV hello Greeting     a rename in place, to a mixed-case name.
  PDMV f01 sub/Moved      a file moved to another directory.
  PDCR fresh / PDWR fresh 700   a new file in the slot the move freed -- written through a node that must NOT be the moved file's stale one.
  PDMV sub/inner sub/Deeper, then sub/Deeper Top   a directory renamed, then moved to the volume directory.
  cwd=/mnt/Top, deep file   pwd climbs out of the moved directory and its file still reads.
  PDMV f04 f05            a rename onto a name that exists replaces it.
  PDMV f02 f02x / sap sapx errno=1   a clear rename bit ($40) refuses: EPERM.
  PDMV ._ext rfork errno=1   a resource fork does not move on its own.
  PDMV sub sub/a/b errno=22  a directory into its own subtree: EINVAL.
  PDTR tree 100000 / sap 300 / ext 0   truncation of a tree, a sapling and an extended file's data fork.
  PDTR f06 70000          a truncate that lengthens.
  PDTR ._ext 0 errno=1    a resource fork is not truncated.

IN THE CHECK SCRIPT (pdrename_check.py): cadius CHECKVOLUME silent (after a control it must flag); every directory whole, with no name twice; each renamed or moved entry at its new place with its old key block, its new name's case word and the backup bit; the moved directory's header named and pointing back; the truncated files' storage types, EOFs and blocks used; and every file byte-identical in cadius's extraction.
